name: A-science-playground
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE high-fidelity desktop WEBSITE SCREENSHOT, 1536x1024 landscape, straight-on, edge to edge without browser chrome, device frame or external annotations. This is SproutLab, an existing English photosynthesis learning app for 10-year-old children. Redesign its active lesson screen, specifically the 'Your turn' phase of 'Sprout's food-making secret'. It is a usable children's learning activity, never a SaaS landing page, marketing page, dashboard, or poster. All text and controls must be large, crisp, correctly spelled and highly legible. Body text approximate 18–22px at this resolution, buttons at least 48px high. One dominant working visual and one obvious next action, compact navigation, very little prose. Show a coherent visual system an engineer could implement with semantic HTML buttons and SVG drawings. The central educational diagram MUST show a whole rooted plant with soil, connected stem and leaves; BLUE water travels INSIDE roots and stem to the leaf, never floating water droplets in air. A labeled magnified leaf slice may show chloroplasts, never a fantasy room or machine in a leaf. Sunlight provides energy. CO₂ enters through a tiny leaf opening. Sprout and Beep can appear as small supporting cartoon characters, with leaves rooted and robot outside the plant. No extra rewards, scores, new quizzes or timers. Show stop 2 of 7, and compact progression labels 'Story', 'Watch', 'Your turn' with Your turn active. Provide a 'Picture notes' link. Sound is optional. Keep the whole core activity and controls inside the screenshot. Avoid the rejected visual formula: warm cream canvas, forest-green chunky rounded headline, green pill navigation, lavender/yellow card grid, long title/subtitle masthead. No giant slogan, feature cards, testimonials, sign-up, pricing, gradient blobs, glassmorphism, gratuitous stickers or decorative dashboard statistics.
DIRECTION A — SCIENCE PLAYGROUND. A distinctive educational exhibit transformed into a clean interactive web lesson. Use saturated COBALT BLUE #214EDB as a purposeful compact top navigation and a narrow left progress rail. BRIGHT WHITE and very pale cool blue are the large diagram grounds, sunshine yellow #FFCD32 for the primary action and learning focus, tangerine for small interaction highlights. Leaf greens are reserved for actual botany. Strong geometric sans with slightly condensed headings and friendly readable body, never bubble lettering. Restrained 2–3px midnight blue outlines, modest 6px corners on real buttons, no card-grid structure, no cream. Layout: 64px cobalt app bar, small white SproutLab wordmark left, 'Map' and 'Journal' links, 'Sound off' control right. Beneath, narrow 100px blue rail displays seven clean numbered stops with 2 active. Main workspace has a compact one-line heading 'Help this leaf make food.' at y100 and a single sentence 'Start by following the water.' Directly below, the drawing covers x180–1010 and y200–810: a beautifully authored bold flat-vector whole plant on a clean white ground, a sunlight cone from upper left, neatly drawn root cross-section lower left, a selected large leaf connected via an annotated magnification line to an enlarged cellular leaf slice on the right of the drawing. Label only 'Roots', 'Stem', 'Leaf', 'A closer look'. The active blue water route is dashed inside the plant. Draw real leaves with engaging organic geometry but clean diagram clarity. A narrow right task area (x1150–1475), open on pale blue ground rather than floating cards, contains '1. Follow the water', one sentence 'Watch it travel from the roots to the leaf.', a bold yellow rectangular button 'Trace the water →', then quieter collapsed steps '2. Let carbon dioxide in' and '3. Add sunlight'. Bottom directly underneath the visual, one understated status strip reads 'Water travels inside the plant.' and small footer 'A simplified model · Not to scale'. Compact phase navigation directly above the drawing: 'Story   Watch   Your turn'. Tiny Beep robot appears at the bottom of task region next to a short speech bubble 'Let’s investigate!'. The visual emphasis is working science diagram and clear next task, crafted joyful interface with comfortable negative space. No physical museum scenery, controls stay conventional web buttons.
